name: Canada
governanceModel: Ambitious state investment without a comprehensive AI statute
debateTopics: Germany-Canada Sovereign Technology Alliance and cross-border AI sovereignty
Scaling 'AI for All's' ambitious 2034 adoption targets
overview:
Canada enters 2026 with enormous AI ambition but no comprehensive AI law. Its proposed statute, the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA), died on the order paper at the January 2025 prorogation and was never revived. In its place, Prime Minister Mark Carney's June 2026 'AI for All' strategy commits roughly $2 billion over five years to sovereign compute, a national public supercomputer, and adoption targets that would take usage from about 12% to 60% of the economy by 2034.

Governance in the meantime runs through existing privacy, human-rights and competition law, a voluntary Code of Conduct for Generative AI, and a Directive on Automated Decision-Making that binds only federal institutions.

debates.summary: Canada has no comprehensive AI statute after AIDA's collapse — 'AI for All' invests heavily but hasn't yet been paired with binding legislation.
debates.expanded: AIDA would have been Canada's first comprehensive AI law, but it died on the order paper when Parliament was prorogued in January 2025 and was never revived. The February 2026 consultation summary signals the government is considering new legislation on safety evaluation, red-teaming, oversight, traceability and liability — but as of mid-2026 none of that exists in force, leaving a real gap between Canada's investment ambitions and its regulatory maturity.

debates.topic: Germany-Canada Sovereign Technology Alliance and cross-border AI sovereignty
debates.summary: A new alliance with Germany, launched at the Munich Security Conference, signals Canada is pursuing AI sovereignty through international partnership rather than going it alone.
debates.expanded: The alliance aims to reduce both countries' strategic technology dependency, notably as Canada's own Cohere moved to acquire Germany's Aleph Alpha in the same period — raising questions about what 'sovereign' AI capability means when flagship national champions are consolidating across borders.

debates.topic: Scaling 'AI for All's' ambitious 2034 adoption targets
debates.summary: The strategy targets adoption growth from roughly 12% to 60% of the economy by 2034 — an extremely steep curve that will require sustained investment well beyond the initial five-year window.
debates.expanded: Independent of the legislative question, delivering on targets of this scale requires sustained compute investment, talent development, and enterprise adoption support far beyond what a single five-year, ~$2B strategy typically sustains — making the plan's multi-decade follow-through a live open question.
